normalized.governing_thought: Fix promotions, shrink and delivery pricing first. Wages are not the main problem, and the 3% target is reachable
executive_summary: What happened: Operating margin fell from 3.37% to 1.02% in two years (operating income $47.9M → $15.3M) even though sales grew 6%. Wages explain only 0.30 of the 2.35-point fall. Gross margin (−1.02 pts: deeper promotions and higher shrink) and e-commerce fulfillment (−0.84 pts) explain ~80%.

Why the draft plan falls short: The 8% labor-hour cut and the e-commerce freeze cannot reach 3%: even if the full $14.5M sticks, margin reaches ~2.0%. If shrink responds as it did in FY2023–25, up to ~$10M leaks back, and FY2026 operating income lands at ~$20M, on the covenant line.

What we recommend: Seven levers worth ~$30M a year (promotion reset, vendor funding, targeted labor, shrink, six store exits at lease end, private label, delivery pricing) take margin to ~3.2% at FY2025 scale for ≤$17.5M one-time cost (cap $25M). Delivery is kept but priced closer to its cost.

What to do first: In the next 90 days: roll out the tested delivery fee chain-wide, drop money-losing promotions and reopen vendor funding, restore receiving and produce checks in low-labor stores, and serve notice on the six stores whose leases end by 2027. FY2026 operating income: ~$27M vs the $20M covenant.
Decisions today: Approve the plan in place of the across-the-board labor cut; approve the delivery-fee change. The other three loss-making stores return to the board for a vote in FY2027.

slides.title: The gross-margin fall is fully explained by deeper promotions and higher shrink, and 38% of promotions lose money

claims.claim: Gross-margin change by driver, FY2023 → FY2025 (pts of sales)
Promotions have grown without paying back
evidence: 38% of FY2025 promotional events lost money even after counting the extra units they sold
funding covered 55% of markdowns in FY2023 but only 46% in FY2025
41% of customers call Harlow "more expensive" (33% in FY2023)

claims.claim: "Promotions work" measures sales, not profit: that is correlation and ignores the lost margin
evidence: the deepest-promotion stores grew comparable sales 1.8% vs 0.2%

claims.claim: The competitive threat is real but local
evidence: ValuMart has opened 11 stores in Harlow trade areas since 2023
Harlow stores within 3 miles had comparable sales of −4.2% vs +1.1% elsewhere

claims.claim: So: keep promotions targeted where ValuMart competes, and cut the events that lose money everywhere else
Promotional sales earn 14 pts less gross margin than regular-price sales; private label earns 12 pts more. Both gaps were unchanged over the period
evidence: promotion effect = +5.0 pts promotional share × 14-pt margin gap; private label = +1.5 pts share × 12-pt premium; shrink = +0.5 pts of sales. Together they equal the −1.02 pts observed

slides.title: Start with four moves the evidence already supports; the structural levers follow within 12 months

claims.claim: First 90 days: Quick, tested, little or no capital
evidence: Delivery pricing: roll out the $7.99 fee / $100 threshold chain-wide; renew the delivery contract while resisting the 3% rise
Promotions: drop the events the post-event review shows lose money; open vendor-funding talks for the next contract cycle
Labor: withdraw the 8% across-the-board cut; restore receiving and produce-rotation hours in Q1 and Q2 stores
Stores: serve non-renewal notice on the six stores whose leases end by 2027

claims.claim: Within 12 months: Build the structural levers
evidence: Labor: store-level labor model; ~3% net hours reduction in high-labor stores
Shrink: theft and receiving-error controls; monthly shrink scorecard by store
Private label: extend the range and use it as the value answer to ValuMart
Stores: exit the six as leases end; 12-month turnaround plan for the other three

claims.claim: By FY2028: Lock in and decide
evidence: Three stores: closure vote at the board in FY2027 if they are still loss-making ($7.5M exit cost)
E-commerce: grow only where each order covers its cost; test basket minimums and click-and-collect incentives
Targets: private label 20.5%, shrink ≤2.3%, promotional share ~26%, margin ≥3.0%

slides.title: Contingency levers worth ~$7.6M cover the main risks, including the 2027 minimum-wage rise

claims.claim: Risks, exposure and mitigation
evidence: ValuMart takes traffic when promotions are cut: Unsized; Harlow comps −4.2% near ValuMart; keep promotions in the 11 ValuMart trade areas; track their comps monthly and restore events if traffic falls
2027 minimum wage +4%: Up to ~$6.7M a year; pass through in prices; productivity from the labor model; draw on contingency levers
Vendors refuse to restore funding: Up to −$4.1M; reward vendors that fund with promotion slots; move volume to private label
Shrink improves more slowly: Each 0.1 pt = $1.5M; monthly shrink scorecard; Q1 stores first
Customers react to labor changes: Unknown (flagged in pack); reallocate rather than cut; watch checkout waits and stock-outs before each wave
Only high-confidence levers deliver: Margin ~2.0% (store exits, fee reset, promotion cut); gross-margin levers are essential: CEO reviews them monthly

claims.claim: Contingency levers ($M a year)
evidence: Exit the other three stores (board vote, $7.5M) +2.2

claims.claim: With these, the plan still clears 3.0% even if the full wage rise lands with no price recovery
evidence: Base $45.6M − $6.7M wage + $7.6M contingency = $46.5M, or ~3.3% of a $1,412M sales base (after nine exits)
wage exposure = 4% on the remaining store labor bill after exits and the targeted cut

slides.title: We ask the board for four decisions today

claims.claim: 1. Approve the margin plan
evidence: Target ≥3.0% operating margin by FY2028; FY2026 plan ~$27M operating income against the $20M covenant. Monthly tracking of the seven levers.

claims.claim: 2. Replace the 8% across-the-board labor cut
evidence: Use a targeted reallocation instead: protect fresh and receiving hours in low-labor stores; ~3% net reduction in high-labor stores.

claims.claim: 3. Approve the chain-wide delivery-fee change
evidence: $7.99 fee and $100 free-delivery threshold, as tested. Delivery stays; e-commerce grows only where orders cover their cost.

claims.claim: 4. Approve a one-time budget of up to $10M, within the $25M cap
evidence: For store exits and the shrink, private-label and promotion programs.
the six lease-end exits need no vote; the other three return for a vote in FY2027 (+$7.5M)

slides.title: Appendix: how the key numbers were calculated

claims.claim: Margin bridge
evidence: The −2.35 pts total = −1.02 gross margin, −0.84 e-commerce, −0.30 labor, −0.20 occupancy, 0.00 other SG&A. $ = pts × $1,503M.

claims.claim: Gross margin
evidence: Promotions +5.0 pts share × −14 pts = −0.70; private label +1.5 × +12 = +0.18; shrink −0.50. Sum −1.02, equal to the reported change.

claims.claim: Labor
E-commerce
Fee reset
Stores
evidence: $3.1M loss removed + $118M × 25% × 12% = $3.5M → $6.6M for nine; × 6/9 = $4.4M; × 3/9 = $2.2M vs $7.5M exit cost.

claims.claim: Promotions and vendors
evidence: The 14-pt gap is read as net of vendor funding: gross markdown ≈ 14 ÷ (1 − 46%) = 25.9 pts on promotional sales; 1 point of funding ≈ 25.9% × 26% × $1,503M × 1% ≈ $1.0M.

slides.title: Appendix: assumptions and judgment calls made in preparing this deck

claims.claim: Plan year: FY2026 is the first plan year and the covenant test year. If FY2026 has already largely run its course, the first-90-day actions matter most for FY2027
Scale: Levers are sized as annual run-rates at FY2025 scale, with no underlying drift
evidence: If promotional creep and e-commerce growth continued at the FY2024–25 pace, operating income would keep falling by ~$15–18M a year, which is why the first wave is urgent.

claims.claim: Lost e-commerce sales: All sales lost from the fee change are treated as new-to-Harlow (the conservative case); some will shift to stores
Store split: benefits are split pro rata. No one-time cost is in the pack for the six lease-end exits; it is covered by the $10M allowance
Implementation budget: $10M one-time allowance is our estimate; the pack does not provide these costs
Promotion and private-label targets are management choices to validate, not forecasts
evidence: Promotional share of ~26% (FY2024 level) and private label of 20.5% (continuing the FY2023–25 trend)

claims.claim: Team claims: The e-commerce 6.1% margin and "promotions work" claims are recomputed or qualified using finance’s data, as shown on pages 4 and 6

normalized.recommendation: Approve the margin plan (seven levers worth ~$30M a year: promotion reset, vendor funding, targeted labor, shrink, six store exits at lease end, private label, delivery pricing) in place of the 8% across-the-board labor cut, targeting ≥3.0% operating margin by FY2028 and ~$27M FY2026 operating income against the $20M covenant; replace the labor cut with a targeted reallocation; approve the chain-wide delivery-fee change ($7.99 fee and $100 free-delivery threshold); approve a one-time budget of up to $10M, within the $25M cap. The other three loss-making stores return to the board for a vote in FY2027.

alternatives_considered.option: Draft plan: 8% across-the-board labor-hour cut and e-commerce freeze
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: cannot reach 3%; even if the full $14.5M sticks, margin reaches ~2.0%; up to ~$10M may leak back through shrink, putting FY2026 operating income at ~$20M, on the covenant line. Labor is 13% of the decline; high customer risk (queues, stock-outs, produce quality); delivery kept, frozen, still loses money. FY2028 run-rate 1.3–2.0%.
Chosen: ~3.2% FY2028 run-rate margin, ~$27M FY2026 operating income (~$7M headroom), fixes main causes, moderate customer risk, one-time cost ~$10M base; $17.5M with 3 stores (cap $25M).
Replace the "freeze" with a rule that volume grows only where each order covers its cost.
Delivery is kept but priced closer to its cost via the tested $7.99 fee / $100 threshold; delivery stays available, so the owners’ commitment is kept.

alternatives_considered.option: Exit the three stores whose leases run beyond 2027 now
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not in base plan: ~$2.2M benefit, $7.5M exit cost, ~3.4-year payback, board vote needed. Given a 12-month turnaround, then closure vote in FY2027 if still loss-making; a contingency lever.

alternatives_considered.option: Exit the six stores whose leases end by 2027
alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen: do not renew; exit as each lease ends; ~$4.4M a year, no exit cost in pack, immediate payback, no vote needed.
